svg.title: Position and verbosity bias in a mock LLM judge, then the fix
svg.desc: A deterministic mock judge scores each answer as quality plus a +1.00 slot-A bonus for going first plus 0.02 points per word. On 12 paired comparisons of system X versus system Y, swapping who goes first flips the verdict on 7 of 12 pairs, a position-bias rate of 0.58. On 5 pairs with tied quality but different length, the longer answer wins all 5, a verbosity-bias rate of 1.00. The naive judge, always showing X first, disagrees with the true higher-quality winner on 5 of 12 pairs, a rate of 0.42. Running both orderings and averaging cancels the slot-A bonus: the corrected judge's position-bias rate drops to 0 of 12, 0.00, and its disagreement with the truth falls to 1 of 12, 0.08. The one surviving error is a verbosity mistake that order-averaging cannot fix, because it corrects where an answer sits, not how long it is.
